title: Integrated Finance Policy: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (2026 Q3 Update)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This integrated finance policy consolidates Redwood Inference’s standards and procedures for annual and quarterly budgeting & forecasting, contracts and legal approval flows, procurement approval and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition and billing practices (ASC 606-aligned guidance). The goal is to provide a single source of truth for finance, product, legal, procurement, and engineering teams to ensure predictable budgeting, compliant contracting, cost-effective procurement, and consistent revenue recognition and invoicing.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood legal entities and business units globally. Includes: expense and capital budgeting, procurement activities (software, cloud, hardware, professional services), contract negotiation and signature, billing and invoicing for hosted API, Dedicated and Private offerings, enterprise contracts, and revenue recognition for subscription, usage, and professional services revenue.

Key definitions:
- Budget owner: individual responsible for delivering against a budget line (usually a manager or product owner).
- Commit: reserved capacity or multi-period contract (e.g., Dedicated capacity commit).
- Vendor onboarding: security, privacy, and procurement checks required before purchase.
- Performance obligation: distinct good/service under ASC 606 for revenue recognition.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
Purpose:
Provide a repeatable cycle for planning headcount, R&D, infra (GPU) spend, sales & marketing, and go-to-market investments while maintaining target operating metrics.
Policy highlights:
- Annual budgeting timeline: budget kick-off (Oct), first draft (Nov), finance review (Dec), executive approval (by Jan 31).
- Quarterly reforecast: teams submit updated forecasts 10 business days prior to quarter start. Material variance (>5% of total budget line or $50k) must include a variance explanation and mitigation plan.
- Budget thresholds: 
  - Manager-level approvals: <= $25k annual spend variance and routine expense item approvals.
  - Director-level approvals: <= $250k annual spend or new vendor engagements under $250k.
  - CFO/Finance Exec: > $250k or capital commitments > 12 months.
Process (high level):
1. Budget owners prepare line-level budgets in the central planning workbook (see template in /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting).
2. Finance consolidates, runs sensitivity scenarios (3 cases), and holds cross-functional alignment sessions.
3. Leadership approves and publishes budgets; variance tracking begins monthly.
Controls and reporting:
- Monthly budget vs actual (BvA) report distributed to owners and leadership.
- SLO: monthly BvA report issued by finance by the 7th business day.

2) Contracts and Legal Process
Purpose:
Ensure that commercial terms, data protection, IP, and liability clauses are reviewed and approved before signature.
Policy highlights:
- Standard templates: Sales Master Subscription Agreement (MSA), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), Statement of Work (SOW), Professional Services Agreement (PSA). Use the latest templates in /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/.
- Contract approval matrix:
  - Sales rep: negotiates commercial terms within playbook limits.
  - Legal Counsel: must review all non-standard term changes, any changes to liability, indemnity, or IP clauses, and all enterprise contracts > $100k ARR.
  - Finance: approves billing schedules, payment terms, and revenue accounting implications for all contracts.
  - Security/Privacy review: required for contracts involving customer data, private deployment (on-prem/VPC), or KMS/HSM integrations.
Execution:
1. Sales files draft contract using approved template in contract management system (CMS).
2. Automatic routing: Legal -> Finance -> Security (if flagged) -> Executive (if contract > $1M or strategic).
3. Signatures: prefer e-signature (DocuSign). Retain executed copies in CMS and a PDF snapshot in the contracts shared drive.
Retention and audit:
- Contracts retained for minimum 7 years after termination.
- Quarterly audit of a sample (10%) of executed contracts for compliance with templates and approvals.

3) Procurement and Vendor Onboarding
Purpose:
Standardize purchasing, ensure vendor risk assessment, and control spend.
Policy highlights:
- Vendor onboarding checklist: legal entity info, SOC 2/ISO27001 or equivalent, data processing terms, insurance certificates, bank/payment info, and procurement P.O. terms.
- Purchase order (PO) policy: POs required for all purchases > $5k. For cloud usage and variable spend, tag and allocate to a cost center or owner.
- Approval thresholds (procurement):
  - Up to $10k: Manager approval.
  - $10k–$100k: Director + Procurement Ops approval.
  - > $100k: VP/Finance Exec approval and legal review.
Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: standard SaaS with SOC 2 and no customer data handling.
- Medium risk: vendors processing customer data or with elevated access (requires security questionnaire and DPA).
- High risk: on-prem deployments, HSM/KMS vendors, or vendors with direct access to production (requires third-party risk assessment and executive sign-off).
Procurement procedure (step-by-step):
1. Requestor submits purchase request via procurement portal with justification, cost center, and required delivery date.
2. Procurement Ops validates vendor onboarding status or initiates onboarding.
3. Approvals routed based on thresholds.
4. PO issued, vendor delivers, accounts payable processes payment per agreed terms.

4) Revenue Recognition and Billing
Purpose:
Ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with accounting standards (ASC 606) and that billing is timely, accurate, and auditable.
Policy highlights:
- Revenue types:
  - Subscription/Commit revenue (hosted or dedicated commits): recognized ratably over the performance period when the customer receives access.
  - Usage revenue (API tokens/embeddings): recognized in the period in which usage occurs.
  - Professional services: recognized based on the satisfaction of performance obligations (time & materials recognized as services delivered; fixed-price SOW recognized by milestone or over time if criteria met).
- Contract modifications: evaluate change in scope or price for distinct performance obligations and apply cumulative catch-up when necessary.
- Billing cadence and terms:
  - Standard customers: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or quarterly in advance for subscription depending on contract.
  - Enterprise customers: invoicing per contract (monthly/quarterly/annual). Payment terms default to Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated and approved by Finance.
  - Late payment: interest at 1.5% monthly (or maximum permitted by law) and escalation to collections after 60 days.
- Credits and refunds: credits for billing disputes must be approved by finance; refunds escalated to Finance Director.
- Deferred revenue and Securitization: all prepayments captured as deferred revenue on the balance sheet and released into P&L per the performance schedule.
Controls and reconciliations:
- Monthly revenue close checklist: invoice issuance, AR aging review, deferred revenue roll-forward, and revenue journal entries.
- SLO: revenue close completed within 6 business days after month-end.
- AR aging: review weekly; past due balances >60 days require collection plan and executive notification.

5) Exceptions and Escalation
- Any exception to approval thresholds or contract templates requires a written variance request submitted to Finance and Legal with rationale and mitigations.
- Escalation path for disputed invoices: Account Owner -> Finance AR -> Legal (if >30 days unresolved) -> Head of Sales/Customer Success -> Executive.

6) Ownership and Contacts
- Finance: responsible for budgeting cadence, forecasting, financial controls, revenue recognition policy (Finance Director: Maria Gonzalez).
- Legal: contract templates, legal review and counsel (Legal Counsel: Jonas Kim).
- Procurement Ops: vendor onboarding and PO issuance (Procurement Lead: Liam O'Connor).
- Security: vendor risk assessments for medium/high risk vendors (Head of Security: Priya Rao).

Appendices and templates:
- Appendix A: Approval matrices (detailed table with thresholds per region and currency).
- Appendix B: Budget template link and forecasting model sample.
- Appendix C: Standard contract templates (MSA, DPA, SOW).
- Appendix D: Vendor onboarding checklist and security questionnaire.

How to comply / quick checklist:
1. Use current templates from the contracts page.
2. Route contracts through the CMS to trigger automatic approvals.
3. Submit purchase requests in the procurement portal and attach onboarding docs for new vendors.
4. Classify revenue types at contract signing and notify Finance of any unusual billing terms.
